judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard consideration/insuring recital; the only defect is the typo 'THES POLICY', which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly 'subject to all the terms of this policy', so it harmonises with the coverage forms and endorsements rather than competing with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely descriptive statement that the policy comprises the listed coverage parts; 'may be subject to adjustment' is vague but non-operative here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Premium Audit condition (Section IV.5 CGL) which provides the adjustment mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Insurance at the described premises applies only for the coverages shown below' is a plain limiting statement, though the blanket schedule that follows is terse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the blanket Limits and CP 00 10 A. Coverage; the blanket-limit presentation could be argued against the per-premises language, but no square conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short schedule note; 'products-completed operations are included, subject to the General Aggregate Limit' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Definition V.16.b.(3) and Section III.2-3, which expressly contemplate classifications making the hazard subject to the General Aggregate Limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple right of the first Named Insured to cancel by written notice; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the duplicate cover-jacket condition and with IL 02 61, which amends only the insurer's cancellation rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 10/30 day structure is precise; only OCR noise mars the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 02 61 (Kansas Changes) expressly replaces this paragraph 2 and adds enumerated cancellation reasons, so the unamended text sits alongside a superseding endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mailing to the last known address is a definite mechanical rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the parallel nonrenewal notice provision in IL 02 61 B.2; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences fixing the effective date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Installment Payments condition, which also speaks of a specified cancellation date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be less than pro rata' is indefinite as to the short-rate calculation, but the operative point (cancellation effective regardless of refund) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses refunds except the Premium Audit return-premium rule, which is compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence evidentiary rule; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim in the second cover jacket and in IL 02 61 B.2; duplication without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause combined with an amendment-only-by-endorsement rule; both limbs are standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is built almost entirely from endorsements that change the forms, which the clause permits; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Audit right limited to books 'as they relate to this policy' during and three years after the period; the boundary is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with the Duties in the Event of Loss provisions permitting inspection of books and records.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is mangled: the disclaimer sentence is broken mid-clause and 'We have the right to' omits the 'but are not obligated' qualifier that appears elsewhere, and 'warrent' is misspelled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duplicate cover-jacket version (c080) states the right differently ('right but are not obligated to') and drops the boiler/elevator carve-out, an inconsistency between two copies of the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates premium responsibility and return premiums to the first Named Insured in two definite limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the CGL Premium Audit condition, which also directs return premium to the first Named Insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anyone having proper temporary custody' is somewhat open-textured, but the transfer bar and death exception are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels Section II.2.c-d of the CGL form, which treats custodians and legal representatives the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming rule of uncertain effect, and the cross-reference to 'Policy Conditions' is imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Cancellation condition and with IL 02 61's Kansas limits on cancellation reasons and notice, which it does not expressly follow.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragmentary applicability line ('cial Property Coverage Part is subject to...'), truncated by scanning rather than drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its function of layering conditions matches the CP 00 10 statements that Loss and Additional Conditions apply in addition to these.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void in any case of fraud' and the intentional concealment limb are strong but standard; 'material fact' is a familiar, workable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (Kansas Changes) expressly replaces this condition with a narrower 'we will not pay' formulation, so two inconsistent versions sit in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Beyond your direction or control' is a familiar standard; the location-by-location breach rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 replaces this condition for townhouse buildings only, leaving a limited, expressly delimited overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single anti-stacking sentence with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Other Insurance condition and the separate Business Income limits; the interaction is conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all of the terms' and the two-year suit limitation are definite on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A replaces this condition with a five-year period, so the policy contains both a two-year and a five-year limitation on suit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 45-day liberalization window and automatic broadening are mechanical and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses adopted revisions; the Changes condition (endorsement-only amendment) is a mild counterpoint but not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR has eaten letters but the rule — no bailee benefits from the insurance — is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the coverage for Personal Property of Others payable 'for the account of the owner', a familiar pairing rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pro-rata and excess limbs are spelled out with a formula; 'covering on the same basis' is slightly open but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Property Not Covered k. (property more specifically described elsewhere) and the excess wording in the Non-Owned Trailers extension; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss or damage commencing' during the policy period and a closed territorial list; both are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Period of Restoration definition states the policy's expiration will not cut short that period, which coexists with this commencement rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses 'Covered Income', a term used nowhere else and undefined in the policy, alongside a waiver list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy elsewhere speaks only of 'Business Income' and 'Rental Value', so the term has no referent in the instrument; CP 01 01 E supersedes it only for Builders' Risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, closely enumerated nuclear exclusion; each limb is tied to defined terms and statutory references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressed to modify Liquor Liability and Auto Coverage Parts that this policy does not contain, a surplusage rather than a conflict, and overlaps the CGL nuclear terrorism endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions are visibly truncated — 'hazardous properties include radioacti... explosive properties' and the source/special nuclear material definition lose their operative words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mangled definitions feed the exclusion in c027 and overlap the CG 21 72 nuclear terrorism definitions, but no substantive contradiction emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Premium computed on rates in effect, recomputed at renewal on rates then in effect; mechanical and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated verbatim later in the jacket and consistent with the Premium Audit condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitlement to a dividend 'if declared' is contingent but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a mutual-company condition attached to a policy issued by the stock company named in the Declarations, a mismatch of issuing entity worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Membership and voting rights are stated with a specific time and place; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Again keyed to State Automobile Mutual, whereas the Declarations name State Auto Property and Casualty Insurance Company as insurer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-assessability statement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against the Calculation of Premium endorsement and Premium Audit, which allow additional earned premium; the tension is mild but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading instruction and pronoun definitions; no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to Section H Definitions of the same form, which exists and is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Direct physical loss of or damage to' is a phrase courts frequently construe, though in a fire claim its application is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage is limited to 'premises described in the Declarations', which must be read with the blanket limits schedule and the Covered Causes of Loss form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed enumerations of Building and Business Personal Property with catch-alls such as 'all other personal property owned by you and used in your business'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with Property Not Covered (c036) and the Declarations' blanket limits; the fit is conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long expressio-unius list containing open items such as property 'more specifically described' in another form and 'other paved surfaces'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item k. interlocks with the Other Insurance condition, and CP 01 01 C.3 adds a further item q. for townhouses, which duplicates the existing paragraph letter q.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to the applicable Causes of Loss Form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations do show the Special Form, so the reference resolves cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An elaborately worked example-driven cap; the arithmetic is explicit and self-illustrating.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Limits of Insurance, which does not list Debris Removal among the additional-limit coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary to move Covered Property... to preserve it' with a 30-day cap; definite enough to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limits of Insurance expressly says payments under this coverage do not increase the limit, an express harmonisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: $1,000 cap, two clear triggers, and an express no-deductible rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limits of Insurance states this limit is in addition to the Limits of Insurance, matching this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pollutants' is a defined term and the $10,000/12-month cap is precise; the testing carve-out is narrow but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Debris Removal's exclusion of pollutant extraction costs and with the Limits provision treating this as additional insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is genuinely obscure — '$10,000 or 5% of the Limit of Insurance... whichever is less' and, for blanket limits, '5% times the value of the damaged building... times the applicable coinsurance percentage' — a formula two parties can plausibly read differently on a blanket policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides the Ordinance Or Law Exclusion (B.1.a) and disclaims the ordinance-cost carve-outs in Loss Payment, Valuation and Replacement Cost 3.f., so its reach against those provisions and the blanket Declarations limit must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tightly drawn electronic data coverage with a $2,500 annual aggregate and detailed cause-of-loss rules.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Keyed expressly to Property Not Covered n. and to the Causes of Loss forms; the cross-references resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A gateway condition requiring a coinsurance percentage of 80% or more; precise, and satisfied by the 100% shown here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Declarations coinsurance entry and the Coinsurance Additional Condition; both are present and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed extension with fixed sub-limits and a three-event termination rule; little room to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 30-day/report-values structure matches the parallel Business Income Newly Acquired Locations extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: $2,500 per premises with a theft carve-out for personal effects; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Covered Property A.1.c (personal property of others) but the payment-for-account-of-owner rule is repeated identically.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Careful separation of additional insurance (lost information) from non-additional costs (blank material and labour); intricate but internally explained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties to Property Not Covered o. and the Electronic Data definition, both consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Temporarily at a location you do not own, lease or operate' has fuzzy edges, but the $10,000 cap and vehicle exclusion are firm.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements the Property in Transit extension in the Special Form, which covers the in-vehicle gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five causes of loss with $1,000/$250 sublimits; expressio unius is intended and plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 D revises '$250' to '$500' for trees, shrubs and plants, so the unamended figure remains in the text alongside the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three cumulative conditions and two exclusions, with a $5,000 cap; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its excess-over-other-insurance rule matches the Other Insurance condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless otherwise indicated' leaves the reader to check each extension, a small indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Some extensions (e.g. Property Off-Premises) do not say whether they are additional insurance, so this catch-all does real work but coheres with the Limits provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Special Form is in fact attached and shown in the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations' is straightforward text, though 'applicable' does the work where blanket limits are used.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with the blanket building/contents/business income limits in the Declarations and with the additional-insurance extensions and Increased Cost of Construction, which sit outside it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The order of operations (coinsurance first, then deductible) is spelled out and illustrated with worked examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Coinsurance condition's own Step (4) deduction of the deductible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line layering statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately describes the relationship among the Common Policy, Commercial Property and Loss Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single categorical sentence barring abandonment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compatible with the Loss Payment option allowing the insurer to take property at an agreed or appraised value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On its face appraisal is unilateral and mandatory ('either may make written demand'), which is precisely the kind of permissive/mandatory question courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 F replaces this condition with one requiring both parties to agree voluntarily to appraisal, so the policy contains two opposite appraisal regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as possible', 'prompt notice' and 'as often as may be reasonably required' are elastic, but they are the standard formulations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored by the Business Income Duties condition, which adds the duty to resume operations; the two are complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurer's four options and the 30-day payment rule are clear; paragraph b. excluding ordinance-or-law increased cost is a pointed limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exclusion runs against the Increased Cost of Construction Additional Coverage, which says the costs addressed in Loss Payment do not include ordinance costs and is not subject to that limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recovery, notice and repayment mechanics are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Transfer of Rights of Recovery condition; no tension found.
